title: Trading book
subtitle: Simulated equity-derivatives book on the S&P 500 and five Mag 7 names: marks, P&L explain, risk, axes
headline: Friday 30 October 2026. The simulated book made +$85k today and +$1.85m since November 2025 on 16 fictitious client trades (12 live). Net vega −$79k per vol point; Corr01 −$65k per correlation point (86% of its limit), so the first axe is to buy correlation.

sections.title: Today's P&L, explained (k$)
paragraphs: Greeks are taken at yesterday's close and applied to today's moves; the unexplained line is what they miss. Delta and its hedge cancel because the desk re-hedges every underlying at the close.

The largest unexplained days are earnings jumps, where a second-order expansion misses the convexity: T12 on 30 Jul (MSFT +15.5%, +$632k); T13 on 31 Jul (AMZN +15.3%, −$190k); T12 on 05 Jun (MSFT -2.7%, +$56k).

sections.title: Risk by underlying
paragraphs: Vega in k$ per vol point, gamma as the P&L of a 1% move, theta per day, after today's deals. Delta is hedged to zero at every close; the column shows what the hedge offsets.

sections.title: Marks: model against live chains
paragraphs: The official mark is the live chain whenever the sister projects captured it that evening. The model mark is kept next to it, as a product-control team would: the gap times the vega is the P&L the remark moved. Single-name gaps are largest around earnings, which a trailing-vol model cannot see.

sections.title: Positions
paragraphs: Every trade is a fictitious client deal; the desk holds the other side. P&L per trade is before delta hedging, which is run across the book.

ideas.thesis: The client puts sold on the S&P 500 leave the desk short index vol with single-name vols unchanged, which is short correlation: the book loses if stocks start moving together, as in a sell-off. The dispersion project measured that risk; this is the desk carrying it.

method: Axes ranked by the share of the risk limit the book uses. Official marks stay at mid; the axe only shifts the price of new deals, by up to one vol point on a single name and half a point on the index at 100% of the limit.
caveats: Simulated book: the trades and clients are fictitious, the market data and the marks are real.

Before the sister projects started capturing option chains (27 Oct 2026), the marks come from models: the S&P 500 ATM history of the vol dashboard and the dispersion project's single-name rebuild from COR1M. That rebuild cannot see earnings, so single-name history is marked too low before results and too high after.
The surface is a parametrisation: an ATM term structure borrowed from the VIX family beyond the live tenors and a linear skew in standardised moneyness, calibrated on the live 25-delta risk reversal.
Variance swaps on single names are marked at ATM x 1.10, the ratio measured on the 50 chains; no cap is modelled.
No funding cost on cash or on the delta hedge, flat 4% rate, constant dividend yields.
